status_definitions.faithful_translation: Checked translation or complete human reconstruction of the cited statement, retaining its explicit hypotheses.
status_definitions.derived_simplification: An additional short consequence of the cited source proof, not asserted to be its named exported statement.
status_definitions.remaining_input: A precisely located arithmetic/construction input whose actual proof has not been reconstructed in this pass.

claims.title: Concrete single-place test datum and three coefficient slots
claims.statement: The local base lattice H(L), source Nsrc(L), target test Ntgt(L), and predual P(L) are explicit integral polynomial lattices. LPprime supplies separated incoming-edge vectors, n >= (1-kappa)dimV, and a matrix pairing identity C Phi u=p^D I, with cStar >= 4(D+1). The normalized pairing is be(F,G)=G(p^Ar F), where w^2=p.
assumptions: The source local ring, Frobenius, weight, lattice and compatibility hypotheses are retained.
For the abstract linear algebra O is a DVR, p is nonzero and nonunit, and the integral coefficient lattices are full.
claims.source_relation: Definitions are translated, not treated as existence proofs. The integral edge/lattice comparisons needed to read the raw LPprime datum as the displayed P-lattice datum are JR12.

claims.title: Primitive pairings force containment of a scaled free module
claims.statement: For an O-linear map phi:A->O^M and nonzero q, if every primitive covector c has a value c.phi(a) dividing q for some a in A, then q O^M is contained in image(phi). Choosing lifts of q times the standard basis gives a linear right inverse up to q, with no finite-generation assumption on A.
assumptions: O is a DVR (the smith_mem source allows a local PID).
q is nonzero in the reconstruction.
Pairings are integral and linear.
claims.source_relation: Complete Smith-basis proof in report section 2; this is a rank/existence argument distinct from v0.2 LC2 tail-to-index.

claims.title: Separated edge blocks assemble without cancellation
claims.statement: Primitive tests supported to p-adic accuracy on one incoming edge give primitive tests on the concatenation. If a divides p^D, then a+p^{D+1}z=a(1+pbz) also divides p^D, because 1+pbz is a unit. Applying JR2 yields LPprimeAt with n=sum_e n_e and matrix C=I.
assumptions: p is nonzero and nonunit.
All normalized edge pairings are integral.
Every primitive combination on each edge has a dual test with value dividing p^D and p^{D+1} divisibility on other blocks.
In the source w^2=p, cStar >= 2(D+1), BePerfect, and dominant weights imply the required off-block integrality.
claims.source_relation: The per-edge tests are still inputs; this is the complete algebraic assembly of those tests.

claims.title: Matrix rank identity bounds bad Smith directions
claims.statement: If integral functionals and generators f_i of a sublattice of rank-d P satisfy C Phi u=qI_n, then some basis of P has at least n indices with q b_a in span(f_i). Split elementary divisors into a_i|q and a_i=q mu_i with mu_i in the maximal ideal; the latter yield qY, and rank(q(I-Y))=n forces at least n good terms. Under LPprime the bad count is <=kappa d.
assumptions: P is a full finite free O-lattice.
q is nonzero.
All tested functionals are integral on P.
For the source application the edge comparisons in JR12 and JR1 are in force.
claims.source_relation: The proof compresses the source jm_count argument by taking fraction-field ranks of the good-term matrix, instead of explicitly constructing an injective map.

claims.title: Neighbor evaluation isolates any good coordinate
claims.statement: For a free action on lattice tuples, delta sections are O-linear and equivariant. Applying y_v to the delta section at an incoming source yields the desired target term once, while all other terms lie in p^{D+1}M_B. Dividing the equivariant pointwise error by p^{D+1} yields an integral section. Tensoring with other integral factors gives p^D delta(tensor) in J_B+p^{D+1}M_B whenever one selected factor has a good index.
assumptions: The acting groups have trivial stabilizers on valid lattice tuples.
Coefficient lattice equivariance, finite neighbor sums, and the normalized integral neighbor-map inclusion hold.
The off-target coefficient values lie in w^cStar times the appropriate target lattice, w^2=p, and cStar >= 4(D+1).
claims.source_relation: The evaluation/cancellation and pointwise-to-section divisibility are reconstructed; the underlying polynomial lattice covariance/integrality is retained separately as JR12.

claims.title: All-bad tensor labels have multiplicative cardinality
claims.statement: If factor v has d_v basis labels with <=kappa_v d_v bad labels, only tensors with every selected coordinate bad need remain exceptional. Their number is <=(product_{v in B}kappa_v)(product_v d_v); all other elementary tensors satisfy JR5. This is a tensor-coordinate argument, not a general bound for arbitrary intersections of bad subspaces.
assumptions: Independent coefficient factors, realized by disjoint polynomial variable blocks.
Integral generating lists of length d_v in each factor, with the selected good/bad properties.
kappa_v is nonnegative for the global application.
claims.source_relation: Complete elementary basis-label proof. The source jLocal only needs spanning lists for this count; independence is supplied separately to compare global ranks.

claims.title: Orbit globalization and Nakayama give the exact RestJ interface
claims.statement: Delta-extend the all-bad tensors over finitely many orbits. Base tensor delta sections are independent by evaluation, so |Omega| product_v d_v <= dna. Their exceptional union has cardinal <=dna product kappa. The local decompositions give p^D M_B <=T+p^{D+1}M_B, with T=J_B+span(C_B); Nakayama gives p^D M_B<=T and hence the exported p^{D+1} inclusion. restJAll and theta_kernel_expansion assemble these proved inputs with the separate walk.
assumptions: Finite orbit set; trivial stabilizers; coefficient lattices full and equivariant.
M_B is a finite O-module and lies in Mna.
p lies in the maximal ideal.
All kappas are nonnegative.
claims.source_relation: dna is the FULL function-module rank, not the retained ramified rank. The lattice walk and the elementary-divisor tail-to-index conversion are not rederived in this fragment.

claims.title: Graph planes supply q0^{r(k-r)} incoming edges
claims.statement: Over residue field F_q0, the kernels of (x,y)->x+A y for A in Mat_{r,k-r}(F_q0) give q0^{r(k-r)} distinct sublattices between pW^k and W^k, all of quotient size q0^r. With the stated per-edge lower bound rho d/q0^{r(k-r)}, summing cancels the denominator; rho<0 is handled by nonnegativity.
assumptions: W is a DVR with uniformizer p and finite residue field of size q0=p^nPrime.
The cancellation application additionally assumes the per-edge bound from JR9.
claims.source_relation: The chart count itself is unconditional under the stated ring hypotheses; the rank-denominator cancellation is conditional on the separate edge-family construction.

claims.title: Type-II single-edge polynomial construction remains an input
claims.statement: For r>=2, EdgeStep must construct enough locally isolated source vectors and primitive dual tests, with source/target height bounds, D1<=CD N k^2 log_p a, and n_e>=(1-Cr N r^2 k/Y)(1-k c0/a)^N dimV/p^{nPrime r(k-r)}. SymbolRealisableBound constructs explicit polynomial lifts involving SPtrue; CloudAt supplies the complementary weight family and valuation-bounded primitive tests. Those polynomial and quantitative proofs are not reconstructed here.
assumptions: All exact Hyps, OrbitHyp, WeightHyp, UnramifiedQuadraticSetting and frame hypotheses in the source.
The absolute-constant and sufficiently-large-C quantifier order of the source is preserved.
claims.source_relation: The report follows the concrete SPtrue formula and identifies genuine primitive-test requirements. It does not mistake conditional package assembly for a proof of the polynomial estimates.

claims.title: Type-I single-edge estimates and averaged kappa remain inputs
claims.statement: The r=1 route uses cleaned lattices CCL and CCLPrime and a pairing-factor lower bound RhoL normalized by dimV/((q0^k-1)/(q0-1)). Its source theorem converts that lower bound into LPprime, and midLP_of handles central-weight changes. The per-edge RhoL construction and the mean-smallness of kappa are not derived by the Type-II argument or by tensor counting.
assumptions: The precise RS, weight, cleaned-lattice, factorization and numerical hypotheses.
The separate source theorem for the required average over weights.
claims.source_relation: This claim prevents the r>=2 Type-II construction from being silently substituted for the r=1 local regime.

claims.title: The same Nakayama argument yields exponent D before weakening
claims.statement: Under the same assumptions and with the same C_B, p^D M_B is already contained in J_B+span(C_B). The source proof establishes this internally before multiplying by p to match the RestJ interface. No downstream walk constants are changed in this reconstruction.
assumptions: Exactly the assumptions of JR7.
claims.source_relation: The main fragment preserves the exported exponent D+1. This optional stronger consequence is not represented as the named exported source statement.

claims.title: Actual integral three-slot comparisons and covariance remain construction inputs
claims.statement: For the actual polynomial coefficient model the base, ball and dual lattices must satisfy base<=ball, dual<=base, w^t ball<=base, w^t base<=dual, and normalized neighbor naturality. Their fixed dimensions/fullness and covariance are also required. Source proofs exist via edge-adapted bases and weight/tensor calculations; this pass uses their precise conclusions and does not reconstruct those polynomial proofs.
assumptions: Exact GAtP, HidaSetting and dominant-weight hypotheses; the source basis and tensor realization.
claims.source_relation: This is deliberately separate from the neighbor cancellation proof JR5 and the tensor count JR6. Those arguments do not by themselves establish naturality of the actual coefficient lattice.
